No web API binds an AES CryptoKey to hardware or to device unlock. The key is protected by origin isolation only. A platform authenticator is present, but WebAuthn gates authentication, not key custody, and cannot wrap or release this key.

Location permission denied or suppressed by this environment.

The Geolocation API exposes no mock-provider flag and no provider identity. A developer-options mock location, a patched browser, or a devtools sensor override is indistinguishable from a real fix. Only weak heuristics remain: implausible inter-fix speed, constant accuracy, and identical repeated coordinates.

No web equivalent of App Attest or Play Integrity is available. The page cannot prove it is unmodified, cannot prove the device is not rooted or emulated, and cannot prevent a modified client from submitting fabricated captures with valid-looking provenance.

Wall clock and monotonic origin agree to 0 ms, but both derive from the same settable device clock. A server-signed time token plus monotonic deltas bounds drift within a session but cannot establish absolute time offline.
Client-enforced TTL evaluates on open and can trigger a shred without the network.
Check-in path works, so revocation lands whenever the device reconnects. Until then the package stays readable.
Web Push cannot be relied on for wipe: iOS requires a home-screen install and user-granted notifications, delivery is best-effort on both platforms, and there is no MDM or OS-level remote-wipe hook.
